Chapter 03 of 19

The Wire Choir

East Van telephone poles / citywide wires90 BPM
The story

Look up in an East Van lane and you will see them: telephone poles, layers of wires, trolley lines, transformers. Add radios, headphones, car stereos and the bass leaking out of a club door, and you have the Wire Choir, the network that carries sound through Terminal City.

Its job is to make sure the right sound reaches the right place. When the mist says a neighbourhood is going quiet, the Choir leans on coincidence. A song comes on at exactly the right moment. The next track streamed to your headphones is not quite the one you expected, and it is better. A recommendation appears. Someone leaves a window open. You still choose what you listen to, and you really did choose it, but the timing was a little too good. There is no DJ and no control room. The Choir only nudges.

It cannot reach everywhere. Inside Stanley Park the signal fades into the trees, which is the Green Static's job. And whatever people make from what they hear, a track, a gathering, a wall of paint, feeds back into the city and keeps it from falling silent. No one hears the broadcast as an announcement. Hum low. Hum high. Bass carries. City knows.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
